STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 


The Tulstram Lakshmi Devi Jaiswal Hospital, Lillooah, Howrah, was 
established under a Trust Deed executed on the 18th February, 1946 by 
Sm. Lakshmi Devi, widow of late Tulsiram Jaiswal. Shri Bandi Prosad 
Jaiswal and Shri Saila Kumar Mukherjee (or_ their successors) . were 
appointed Trustees. ‘Fhe said Trust Deed provided for the establishment 
of a hospital with 50 heds, the number being increased to 500 within a 
period of seven years from the date of the establishment of the hospital. 
It also provided for the establishment of a Medical College. 


The ‘Irustees have not, however, been able to estahlish a Medical College 
or to provide the stipulated number of beds. They have been maintaining 
40 beds only. They took up construction of a multi-storied building for 
expansion of the hospital but could not make any progress for want of funds. 
The Trustees accordingly approached the State Government with a proposal 
to take over the hosp‘tal with its assets and liabilities for expansion, 
improvement and -muaintenance, excluding the ‘‘Busu Memorial Leprosy 
Clinic’’ which is located in the hospital compound but is separate from the 
hospital. 

In a congested industrial area hke Howrah there is urgent need for 
increasing oxisting hospital facilities. According to estimate there should 
be about 600 hospital beds but there are only 252 beds in the Howrah 
General Hospital. 

With a view, therefore, to making provision for an adequate number of 
beds to meet the requirements of the locality by expanding and improving 
the Tulsiram Lukshmi Devi Jaiswal Hospital] it is proposed to take over the 
institution through legislation aud run it as a State institution. 


The Bill has been drafted with that object in view. 


J. R. DHAR, 


Member-in-charge. 
CaLcotTtTa, 


The 23rd March, 1962.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 


This Bill is introduced in pursuance of article 20401) of the Constitution 
of India, read with article 206 thereof, to provide for the appropriation out of 
the Consolidated Fund of West Bengal of the moneys required to meet the 
expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund and the grants made in advance 
by the Assembly in respect of the estimated expenditure of the West Bengal 
Government, for a part of the year ending on the thirty-first day of March, 1963. 


2. Under the Constitution of India no money can be withdrawn from the 
Consolidated Fund of West Bengal except under appropriation made by law.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 
The object of the Bill is to provide for the appropriation out of the 
Consolidated Fund of West Bengal of the moneys required to meet— 
(a) the supplementary or additional grants made by the Assembly; and 


(6) the supplementary or additional expenditure charged on the 
Consolidated Fund of West Bengal, but not exceeding, in any case, 
the amount shown in the statement previously laid before the House 
in pursuance of article 205(7) of the Constitution of India 


for the services and purposes of the year 1961-62. 


2. Under the Constitution of India no money can be withdrawn from the 
Consolidated Fund of West Bengal except under appropriation made by law.

(2) In the respective areas under the fixed-fee system of pachwai, the 
difterence between the basic price of rice fixed by Government and the 
uverage price of rice per quintal, multiplied by the quantity on which 
license fee is to be assessed, shall be added to or subtracted from the amount 
of license fee prescribed for each entry in the scales according as the average 
price of rice in any particular month is below or in excess of the basic 
price of rice per quintal. The average price of rice in a month shall be 
the average of the prices per quintal calculated from the figures published 
in the ‘‘Caleutta Gazette’ for all the weeks in the month. The price pre- 
valent at the Subdivisional headquarters shall be applicable to all the shops 
within the subdivision.

(b) The Excise Conimissioner may, in his diseretion and by an order in 
writing, permit relaxation of clause (a) for good and sufficient reasons.

his license pay, for due observance of the conditions and terms of the license, 
an advance equivalent to one month's license fee which was payable during 
the previous year.

proof litre for the purpose of payment of license fees as above, whenever

disregarded. ;

of country spirit taken by the licensee on and from Ist April 1962 and shall 
be paid by the 15th of the month following unless in any particular case 
Or on any particular occasion, the Collector or the Superintendent of Excise 
directs otherwise.

writing permit relaxation of clause 1৪) for good and sufficient reasons.

No. 346Ex.—22nd March 1962.—In supersession of orders issued under 
the Forest and Excise Department (Excise) memorandum No. 536-Ex/48- 
19/44, dated the 9th January 1945, the undersigned is directed by order of 
the Governor to say that the Governor is pleased to sanction the grant of 
rebate, according to the scale prescribed below, in lincense fees payable by 
the retail vendors of country spirit in West Bengal except in— 


(3) the district of Calcutta; 


(it) the subdivision of Asansol (excluding police-station Khaksa) in the 
district of Burdwan; 


(111) the areas where country spirit of 77.5° under-proof strength is 
issued and license fees are levied thereupon according to the 
separate scale of license fees prescribed therefor; and 


(iv) the district of Purulia and the police-stations of Chopra, Islampur, 
Goalpokhar and Karandighi in the district of West Dinajpur.

PART 111 —Acts of the West Bengal Legislature 
GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 
LAW DEPARTMENT 
Legislative 
NOTIFICATION 


March, 1962.—The following Act of the West Bengal Legislature, 


No. 694L.—29th 


assented to by the Governor, is hereby published for general information: — 


West Bengal Act II of 1962 


THE WEST BENGAL APPROPRIATION (VOTE ON 
ACCOUNT) ACT, 1962. 


{Passed by the West Bengal Legisilature.} 


{Assent of the Governor was first published in the Calcutéa Gazette, 
Extraordinary, of the 29th March, 1962.) 


An Act to provide for the withdrawal of certain sums from and 
out of the Consolidated Fund of West Bengal for a part of 
the year ending on the thirty-first day of March, 1963. 


WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the withdrawal of 
certain sums from and out of the Consolidated Fund of West 
Bengal for a part of the year ending on the thirty-first day of 
March, 1963; 


It is hereby enacted in the Thirteenth Year of the Republic 
of India, by the Legislature of West Bengal, as follows:— 


1. This Act may be called the West Bengal Appropriation 
(Vote on Account) Act, 1962. 


2. From and out of the Consolidated Fund of West Bengal 
there may be withdrawn sums not exceeding those specified in 
column 2 of the Schedule amounting in the aggregate to the 
sum of rupees seventy-eight crores, twenty-eight lakhs and one 


* thousand towards defraying the several charges which will come 


in course of payment during the year ending on the thirty-first 
day of March, 1963. 


3. The sums authorised to be withdrawn from and out of 
the Consolidated Fund of West Bengal by this Act shall be 
appropriated for the services and purposes expressed in the 
Schedule in relation to the said year.

NOTIFICATION 


No. 2190/MIM-70/60. — 28th March 1962.— 
Whereas Government in their notification No. 437 / 
MIM-30/55, dated the 14th January 1956, published 
in the ‘Calcutta Gazette Extraordinary’, dated the 
16th January 1956, issued an order under section 67A 
of the Bengal Municipal Act, 1932 (Bengal Act XV 
of 1932), declaring that the Kanchrapara municipality 
in the district of 24-Parganas shall have an Executive 
Officer for a period of two years, with effect from the 
date of appointment of such an Officer; 


And whereas in Government notifications— 


No. 581 /MIM-30/55, dated the 15th January 1958, 
No. 3001 /MIM-14/58, dated the 27th March 1958, 
No. 384/MIM-14/58, dated the 14th January 1959, 
No. 333 /MIM-14/58, dated the 14th January 1960, 
No. 7358 /MIM-14/58, dated the 13th July 1960, 
No. 348 /MIM-14/60, dated the 14th January 196l, 
and 
No. 192/MIM-70/60, dated the 15th January 1962, 
published in the “Calcutta Gazette Extraordinary”, 
dated the 16th January 1958, 28th March 1958, 14th 
January 1959, 14th January 1960, 14th July 1960, 14th 
January 1961 and 15th January 1962, respectively, 


the said period of appointment was extended up to 
the 3lst March 1962; 


1413 


1414 ۲188ء‎ CALOUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINAR iI. [(PangI

ےکپچووص×سب ےچ چجژڑٹچتگگ گے ু্- সু স্সু- শু‏ —— 


And whercas, in the opinion of the Governor, 
further extension of the said period of appointment is 
necessary; 


Now. therefore, in exercise of the power conferred 
by sub-section (1) of section 67۸ of the said Act, 
the Governor is pleased to extend the period of 
appointment of the Executive Officer for a further 
period of two months from the Ist April 1962. 


2. In exercise of the power conferred by sub- 
sections (2) and (3) of section 67A of the said Act 
the Governor is further pleased to appoint Shri 
N. C. Ukjl, retired Sub-Deputy Collector, to continue 
during the said extended period as the Executive 
Officer of the said municipality and to direct that he 
Shall continue to exercise and perform the powers 
and duties conferred and imposed upon him by 
Government notification No. 10390/MIM-70/60, 
dated the I2th September 1960.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS 


The living conditions of labour employed in the iron 
ore mining indust are not satisfactory. A Working 
Group set up in 1956, which included representatives of 
employers und workers, while commenting on __ the 
unsatisfuctory labuur conditions in mines surveyed by them, 
recommended that a welfare fund financed by a special cess 
should be set up on the pattern of the Coal Mines Labour 
Welfare Fund or the Mica Mines Labour Welfare Fund. 
This recommendation has also been supported by the 
tripartite Industrisl Committee on mines other than coal, 
which included representatives of State Governments. It 
is not the intention to take over completely the responsibility 
of the employers in the matter of provision of welfare 
facilities, but it is proposed to levy a cess on all iron ore 
produced and to utilize the proceeds of the cess for provid- 
ing labour employed in the iron ore mines with welfare 
facilities comparable to those now being provided in the 
coal and mica mines. The Bill seeks to give effect to these 


proposasls. 
; G. L. NANDA. 
New Deru; 

The 21st November, 1961. 


FINANCIAL MEMORANDUM 


Clause 2 of the Bill provides for the levy of a cess at 
such rate not exceeding 50 naye paise per metric tonne of 
iron ore produced, as the Centra] Government may fix from 
time to time. It is expected that the cess at the maximum 
rate of 50 naye pnise per metric tonne will yield about 
rupees forty lakhs per annum. After meeting the expenses 
incurred on Advisory Committees, etc., the balance will be 
utilized, subject to appropriation by Parliament, on the 
objects specified in clause 3 of the Bill,

MEMORANDUM REGARDING DELEGATED 
LEGISLATION 


Clause 8 of the Bill empowers the Central Government 
to make rules for carrying into effect the purposes of the 
Act. Matters in respect of which such rules may be made 
are specified in that clause. They inter alia relate to the 
collection of the cess and the determination of the cost of 
such collection, the manner in which the amount of the cess 
is to be applied, the conditions governing the grant oi 
moneys to State Governments, etc., m aid of any approved 
schemes, the standard of welfare facilities to be maintained 
by mine managements for purposes of obtaining grants and 
the limits to be imposed on such grants, and the composition 
of the Advisory Committees. Rules made under this clause 
may also provide that a breach of any such rule shall be 
punishable with fine. 


The scope of clause 8 is thus limited to matters of 
procedure or detail and the delegation is of a normal 
character.

Bengal, the High Court, Goverpment Treasury, etc. 


GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


OFFICE OF THE COMMISSIONER OF POLICE 
CALCUTTA 


ORDER 
Dated the 3lst March 1962 


Whereas, I, S. M. Ghosh, Commissioner of Police, 
Calcutta, am of opinion that it is necessary for the 
purpose of preventing annoyance to, and injury to 
the health of, the public, and for the purpose of 
maintaining public peace and _ tranquillity, to 
prohibit, restrict, regulate and impose conditions on 
the use or operation, in any area within the town 
of Calcutta and the suburbs of Calcutta (as 
respectively defined in the Calcutta Police Act, 1866, 
and notification under section 1 of the Calcutta 
Suburban Police Act, 1866), or in any vehicle within 
such areas. of microphones, loudspeakers or other 
apparatus for amplifying human voice or amplifying 
music or other sounds; 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers con- 
ferred on me by section 43D(1Xa) of the Calcutta 
Police Act, 1866, and section 17D(lXa) of § the 
Calcutta Suburban Police Act, 1866, read with the 
Calcutta and Suburban Police (Amendment) Act, 


1433 


14384 THE CAI.CUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRAORDINARY, [Parr ও 
MARCH 31, 1962. 


en শা পপি 


1957 (West Bengal Act XX of 1957), I, the said 
S. M. Ghosh, Commissioner of Police, Calcutta, do 
hereby order: — 


(1) That no person shall use or operate in any 
area mentioned in the schedule below, 
m.crophone, loudspeaker, or other . 
apparatus for amplifying human voice or 
amplifying music or other sounds without - 
prior permission in writing of the Commis- 
sioner of Police, Calcutta, and subject 
to such conditions as the Commissioner of 
Police, Calcutta, may deem fit to impose; 


(2) that no person shall use or operate in any 
vehicle in any such area microphones, loud- 
speakers, or other apparatus for amplifying 
human voice or amplifying music or other 
sounds, without prior permission in writing 
of the Commissioner of Police, Calcutta; 


(3) nothing in this order shall apply to any 
apparatus or vehicle belonging to Govern- 
ment or to such organisations as may from 
time to time be specified by the Com- 
missioner of Police, Calcutta, in this 
behalf; 


(4) nothing herein contained in orders 1, 2 and 3 
above shall affect the existing orders of the' 
Commissioner of Police, Calcutta, prohibit- 
ing or restricting music and the making of 
other noises, before hospitals or mosques. 
or in areas where sounding of horns 25 
prohibited. 


Schedule 


The town of Calcutta as defined in Calcutta Police 
Act, 1866, together with suburbs of Calcutta as 
defined by notifications under section I of the 
Calcutta Suburban Police Act, 1866. 


S. M. GHOSH, 
Commissioner of-Police, Calcutta.

Pradesh, Madras, Mysore, Maharashtra, Orissa, 
Punjab, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal

ELECTION COMMISSION, UNDIA 
NOTIFICATIONS 
New Delhi, the 6th April 1962. 
No. 479/62.—Whereas the term of office of 


Dr. Rajendra Prasad, President of India, is due to 
expire on the 12th May 1962: 


And whereas under sub-section (3) ot section 4 
of the Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections 
Act, 1952, the Election Commission is required to 
appoint dates for the Presidential election so that it 
will be completed at such time as will enable the 
President thereby elected to enter upon his office on 
the 13th day of May 1962: 

Now, therefore, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of 
section 4 of the said Act, the Election Commission 
hereby appoints in respect of the said election— 

(a) the 16th April 1962, as the last date for 

making nominations; 

(b) the 18th April 1962, as the date for the 

scrutiny of nominations; 

{c) the 2lst April 1962, as the last date for the 

withdrawal of candidatures; and 


(d) the 7th May 1962, as the date on which a 
poll shall, if necessary, be taken. 
By order, 
PRAKASH NARAIN, 
Secy. to the Election Commission.

he tuken into consideration on or after the 15th July

before that date will be duly considered.

physical (anatomical, physiological, and functional) 
und mental capacity for the exercise of the necessary 
functions of a normally occupied life which would 
be expected in a healthy person of the same age and 
sex. For such assessment, recognised  cardio- 
respiratory function tests shall be used 10 assess the 
degree of cardio-respiratory function impairment. 


(2) It shall be determined whether the disablement 
is temporary or permanent and also the percentage 
loss of function as it pertains to the lost of working 
capacity for receiving compensation. 


(3) Assessment of disablement — shall be pro- 
portionate to the loss of earning capacity, total 
disablement being taken to be 100 per cent. loss of 
carning Capacity. 


Explanation: For the purpose of 0015 rule, 
‘permanent disablement” 51811 mean such disable- 
ment as is certified to be permanent by the Medical 
Board. 


7. Certification of cases—{!) The claims for 
compensation of any workman contacting a disease 
specified in Part C of Schedule III to the Act shall 
be supported by a certificate issued by a qualified 
medical practitioner: 


Provided that where the contacting of such disease 
has resulted in permanent disablement, such ٣ 
shall be supported by a certificate issued by the 
Medical Board. 


(2) The certificate issued by a qualified medical 
practitioner shall contain the following particulars:—

A. Constitution of Pneumoconiosss Medical 
Board. (1) The State Government shall constitute 
a Pneumoconiosis Medical Board for the conduct of 
inedical examinations, Submission of medical reports 
and the yrant of medical certificates in pursuance of 
these rules: 


Provided that with respect to workmen employed 
in mines, the State Government may recognise uny 
Medical Board for the purpose of these rules. 


(2) The Board constituted or recognised under sub- 
rule (1) shall consist of three qualified medical 
practitioners of whom one shall be a radiologist. 


5. Medical conditions under which pneumo- 
coniosis may be considered to be an occupational 
disease.—{1) The diagnosis of pneumoconiosis shall 
be carried out with all the necessary technical 
guarantees. Proof of the degrec of development of 
the pathological or anatomical changes in the 
respiratory and cardiac systems shall be furnished 
by the radiographic record and other labdratory 
records, which shall be accompanied by the report 
of a full clinical examination, including a report of 
the industrial history of the person concerned, the 
record of all occupations in which he _ has been 
employed, the nature of the harmful dusts to which 
he was exposed and the duration of such exposure. 


(2) For entitlement to compensation, silicosis and 
coal-miners’ pneumoconiosis shall fulfil the following 
radiological and clinical conditions:— 


(a) The radiological examination of the workman 
must reveal— 


(i) the appearance of generalised micronodular 
or nodular fibrosis covering a considerable 
part of both lung fields’ whether 
accompanied or not by signs of pulmonary 
tuberculosis, or 


(11) in addition to a marked accentuation of the 
pattern of both lungs, the appearance of 
one or several pseudotumoral fibrotic 
formations, whether accompanied or not 
by signs of pulmonary tuberculosis, or 


(111) the appearance of both of these types 
of fibrotic lesions at once, whether 
uccompanied or not by signs of pulmonary 
tuberculosis; 

(b) Serial radiological pictures taken over a 
period during periodical medical examina- 
tions shall, as far as possible, be considered 
in making definite diagnosis in cases where 
doubt exists; 

(c) Radtolopical interpretation shall be based on 
the standard International classification laid 
down by the International Labour Organisa- 
tion (Geneva classification); 


(d) The Clinical examination of the workman 
concerned must reveal a decrease or 
detcrioration of the respiratory function or 
cardiac function, or a deterioration of the 
State of general health, caused by the 
pathological processes specified above.

LAW (JUDICIAL) DEPARTMENT 


RESOLUTION 


No 2619J.—i7th April 1962.—The State Government have received with 
deep regret the news of the death of Shri M. N. Ghosh, Barnater-at-Law, 


lately Additional Deputy Lega) Remembrancer, West Bengal, on Thursday, 
the 29th March 1962. 


On account of his standing and experience Shr Ghosh was appointed as 
Additional Deputy Legal Remembrancer, West Bengal, in 1965 and workea 
as such until his demise on the 29th March 1962 in harness. 


As Additional Deputy Legal Remembrancer Shri Ghosh upheld the 
highest traditions of the public service in respect of integrity and devotion 
to duty. Huis sense of fairness, pleasing manners und impressive personality 
earned for him the esteem of all who came in contact with him. 


The Government of West Bengal place on record their profound sorrow 
and sense of loss on the passing away of an able lawyer and a dutiful anid 
etticient law officer and convey to hia family their sincere condolences. 


By order of the Governor,

MINISTRY OF FOOD AND ACRICULTURE 
(Department of Food) 
ORDER 
New Delhi, the 17th March 1962 


G.S.R. 374.—In exercise of the powers conferred by section 3 of the 
Essential Commodities Act, 1955 (10 of 1955), the Central Government 
hereby makes the following Order, namely ہے‎ 


1, Short title, extent and commencament.—(1) This Order muy be 
called the Roller Mills Wheat Products (Price Control) Order, 1962. 


(2) It extends to the States specified in Schedule | to this Order, 
(3) 1t shall come into force at once. 


2. Definitions.—Jln this Order, unless the context otherwise requires,— 


(a) “Greater Bombay’’ meaus the area in the State of Maharashtra 
lying within the jurisdiction of the Municipal Corporation of 
reater Bombay; 


(b) “‘roller mill’? means a flour mill in which disintegration of wheat is 
done by grooved steel or iron rollers worked by power; 

(c) ‘‘wheat products’’ means suji (or rawa), maida, wholemeal atta or 
resultant atta, produced in a roller mill. 


3. Maximum Ex-mill prices of wheat products.._No owner or other 
person 11) sue of a roller mill shall sell, or offer for sale, ex-mill any of 
the wheat products specified iu column 1 of Schedule IJ to this Order,— 


(a) in the States of Assam, Orissa und West Bengal and in Greater 
Bombay, ut a price exceeding the price specified against it in 
column 2, or where the metric system of weights is not in force, 
in column 3 of the said Schedule; 


(b) in the State of Maharashtra (excluding Greater Bombay) und in 
any other Stute [not being a State specified in sub-clause (a)], 
to which this Order extends, at a price exceeding the price 
specified against it in column 4, or where the metric system 
of weights is not iu force, in column 5, of the Schedule 
aforesaid.

Explanation.—The prices referred to in this clause are— 
(1) exclusive of-— 


(a) the pro rata amount of octroi, 1f any, paid by the mill in respect 
of wheat used in the manufacture of the wheat products, 


(b) the sales tax, if any, payable by the seller; 


(ii) for gross weight inclusive of the cost of the bag, but where wheat 
products are sold in cloth bags in quantities of 40 kg., 20 kg., 
and 10 kg., a sum of 70 nP., 37 nP., and 19 nP. respectively 
may be charged in addition to the said prices. 


4. Sales at mill depots and by selling agents.—The maximum ex-mill 
prices referred in clause 3 shall ulso apply to sales, other than sales direct 
to consumers at mill depots und to sales by sole-selling agents of a mill.

NOTIFICATION 


New Delhi, the 3186 March 1962 


In exercise of the powers conferred by section 169 of the Representu- 
tion of the People Act, 1951 (43 of 1951), the Central Government, after 
consulting the Election Commission, hereby makes the following further 
amendments in the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, namely :— 


Short titlo. 1. These rules may be called the Conduct of Elections (Second 
Amendment) Rules, 1962. 


In rule 70 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 (hereinafter‏ .2 اس سا 
ment 0‏ 
rule‏ 


70 called the said rules), in rule 38A, after sub-rule (1), the following sub- 
"rules shall be inserted, namely :— 


(18) At the time of issuing a ballot paper to an elector, the polling 
officer shall record the serial number thereof against the entry relating 
to the elector in the copy of the electoral roll set apart for the purpose. 


(1B) Save as provided in sub-rule (1A), no person in the polling 


station shall note down the serial numbers of the ballot papers issue 
to particular electors.” 


Amend- 3. In rule 98 of the said rules, in sub-rule (1), for the words “01 a 
ment of competent court or tribunal”, the words ‘‘of the Election Commission or 
’ of a competent court or tribunal’’ shall be substituted.

NOTIFICATION. 


No. 2528A.R.—10th April 1962.—Whereas nine of 
the members of the West Bengal Legislative Council 
elected to that House by the members of the West 
Bengal Legislative Assembly will be retiring on the 
4th June 1962, on the expiration of their term of 
office;

Representation of the People Act, 1951 (XLIII of 
1951), the Governor is pleased hereby to call upon 
the members of the West Bengal Legislative Assem- 
bly to elect, in accordance with the provisions of the 
said Act and of the rules and orders made there- 
under, nine members to fill the seats of 05 said 
retiring members of the West Bengal Legislative 
Council, before the 3lst May 1962, which is the date 
appointed in this behalf by the Election Commission. 


By order of the Governor, 


P. K. BOSE, Dy. Secy. to the 
Govt. of West Bengal.

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 
HOME DEPARTMENT 
Press 
NOTIFICATION 


No. 474Pr./13/62 Pt. l1.—Illth April 1962.—Where- 
as it appears to the Governor that the book in Hindi 
entitied ‘“‘Monohar Kahaniya” published by 05 
Ashoke Pustak Mandir of 163 Mahatma Gandhi 
Road, Calcutta, contains an article named 
“Muhammed Sahib Ka Ansoo” (along with a 
pictorial representation purporting to be that of 
Prophet Mohammed) which contains matters which 
are deliberately and maliciously intended to outrage 
the religious feelings of the Muslims, a class of 
citizens of India, by insulting their religion and 
religious beliefs and the publication of which is 
unishable under section 295A of Indian Penal Code 
Act XLV of 1860); 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the power conferred 
by section 99A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 
1898 (Act V of 1898), the Governor is pleased hereby 
to declare every copy of the said book and all other 
documents containing copies, reprints and translations 
of, or extracts from, the said article along with the 
said pictorial representation, to be forfeited to 
Government. 


By order of the Governor, 
.کا‎ N. SEN GUPTA, 
Dy. Secy. to the Govt. of West Bengal.

write on it the name of the person he votes for the office of the 
President or the Vice-President, as the case may be. He shall 
then fold the slip and hand it over to the President, 

(b) The President shall then count the number of votes secured by 
vach nominee and declure the member who secures the largest 
number of votes to be duly elected as President or ae 
President, as the case may be. 

(c) 11 equal number of votes is secured by two or more nominees for 
either the office of the [resident or the Vice-President, che 
President may then make the elections by lot drawn in such 
manner as he thinks fit, and the persons so elected by lot shall 
be declared as duly elected President or the Vice-President, as 
the case may be.

the grant so made by the State Government, if any, at the end of the 
financial year instead of refunding it, for utilisation in subsequent year. 


(2) All applications for grant from the State Government shall be made 
through the Director of Veterinary Services of the Government of West 
Bengal. Each auch application shall invariably accompany a statement of 
estimated expenditure and the income of the Council and the audit report 
of the Council for the previous year: 


Provided that for the grant for the financial year in which the Council 
is constituted for the first time it shal] not be necessary to submit the audit 
report of the Council : 


Provided further that all applications for grant from the State Govern- 
ment shall be made by the President of the Council. 


(3) The grant that may be sanctioned by the State Government shall 
be drawn by the 66 of the Council in T. R. Form No. 48 after it 18 
duly countersigned by the sanctioning authority. 


(4) There shall be maintained a register of grant, that may be made 
by the State Government, showing the amount sanctioned, date of drawal, 
amount of expenditure incurred and the balance, if any, at the end of the 
financial year.

Miscellaneous 


Validity of tee order of the Secretary or the Rogistrar or the President or 
the Counctt 


66. The action taken by the Secretary or Registrar or the President 
in accordance with the provisions of these rules shall on no account be held 
to be void: 


Provided that any question that may arise as to the validity of the 
decision taken by the Secretary or Registrar or by the President ehal] be 
decided by the President or the Council as the case may be: 


Provided further that any question that may arise as to the validity 
of the decision of the Council shall be referred to the State Government and 
its decision thereon shall be final.

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


EDUCATION DEPARTMENT 


NOTIFICATION 


No. 1372-Edn(G).—19th April 1962.—Whereas the 
Senate of the Calcutta University has submitted to 
the Chancellor for her approval Statutes framed by 
the Senate in respect of colleges recognised by or 
affillated to the University and embodied in the 
proposed “College Code”; 


And whereas the Chancellor, in pursuance of the 
provisions of sub-section 5 of section 34 of § the 
Calcutta University Act, 1951, sought the advice of 
the Minister-in-charge of the Department of Edu- 
cation of the Government of West Bengal, whom the 
Chancellor is required to consult before according 
her approval to the said Statutes; 


And whereas the said Statutes deal, among other 
things, with matters like— 


(1) qualification of teachers. 
(2) hours of work of teachers. 
(3) age of retirement of teachers, 


(4) scales of pay for different categories of 
teachers. 


(5) terms of appointment, 
(6) maintenance of Service Books for teachers. 


(7) rights and duties of teachers and rules of dis- 
cipline governing them. 


1629 


1630 THE CALCUTTA GAZEITE, EXTRAORDINARY, جتھ۲]‎ I 
APRIL 23, 1962 


a ay 


(8) Teachers’ Council, 
(9) Provident Fund. 
(10) Leave Rules. 
(11) Governing Bodies; 


And whereas it is considered necessary to enquire 
into the conditions’ prevailing in recognised 
or afliliated colleges of different categories for the 
purpose of ascertaining whether it is advisable or 
feasible to introduce or enforce uniformity in matters 
such as those provided for in the College Code 
by the framing of Statutes and, if so, to what 
extent and also the extent to which discretion or 
autonomy in respect of all or any of these matters 
should remain with the authorities responsible for 
the management of such colleges; 


And whereas the Governor is of the opinion that 
it is necessary to appoint a Commission for making 
an enquiry into the aforesaid matters which’ are 
matters of definite public importance; 


Now, therefore, the Governor, in exercise of the 
power conferred by section 3 of the Commission of 
Enquiry Act, 1952, is pleased hereby to appoint a 
Commission consisting of one member, namely, Shri 
Phani Bhusan Chakravartti, retired Chief Justice of 
the High Court at Calcutta, to enquire into the afore- 
said matters and to make recommendations to the 
State Government within four months from the date 
of this notification, including recommendations for 
such amendments to the Calcutta University Act, 
1951, as may be necessary to enahle the Senate of 
the Calcutta University to frame Statutes relating 
to those of the said matters which it may be found 
desirable and practicable to control بط‎ Statute: 


The Governor, in exercise of the powers conferred 
by section 5 of the Commissions of Enquiry Act, 
1952, 1s also pleased hereby to direct that the 
provisions of sub-section (2), sub-section (3), sub- 
section (4) and sub-section (5) of the said section 
Shall apply to the Commission. 


By order of the Governor,

Company represented their grievances before’ the

The Company deniés the allegation of the Union 
that thé workmen under reference ever incurred the 
displeasure of the management for any Union. acti- 
vities. The 21 workmen under reference were 
charge-sheeted for various offences to which they 
gave their explanations. The Company alleges that 
enquiries were held against all these workmen and 
that after proper enquiries the workmen having been 
found guilty of the offences they were char with 
were dismissed from service, that ٤ا‎ action of the 
Company was just and proper and that there was no 
violation of principles of natural justice. 


Decision 


The Union in its brief written statement merely 
stated that the workmen under reference incurred 


the displeasure of the management of the Company 


for representing the grievances of the employces of 
the Company, that they were victimised for their 
Union activities and that the action of the manage- 
ment .was wholly illegal, mala fide, and against all 
principles of natural justice. The Union admits that 
the workmen under reference were charge-sheeted 
by the Company to which ,they. gave their replies. 
The Union does not say, that there were no enquiries 
at all, but it says that there were “practically no 
17100111865” and its contention is that the Company’s 
action was illegal. The Union does not state any- 
where in the written statement as to the exact 
nature of the charges, the specific denials and 
allegations of the workmen under reference and 
Specific instances of commission of mistakes or 
errors or omission to observe the rules of procedure 
in holding the enquiries and dismissing the work- 
men. There is merely a repeatation of the stock 
phrase—‘‘violation of principles of natural justice’. 


The Company, on the other hand, has given a 
statement containing all the necessary particulars tn 
respect of the charges against each of the workmen 
under reference. 


Both the parties, adduced evidence and it was sub- 
mitted by the 0 at the time of hearing that 
serial No. 3, Rudra Protap and No. 16, Moni Sankar 
Shaw, having withdrawn from the dispute, their 
cases need not be gone into and the Union prayed 
that a ‘no-dispute’ award might be passed in respect 
of these two workmen. 


Both parties submit that the cases of serial 
Nos. 1, 2, 14, 17, 18 and 20 may be considered 
individually and there are two groups of workmen 
whose cases may be considered collectively—one 
group consists of serial Nos. 4 to 13 and the other 
group of serial Nos. 15, 19 and 21. 1 will 10৬7 0155 
up the cases of workmen serial Nos. ,ا‎ 2, 14, J7, 18 
and 20, individually, and the cases of two groups 
separately:

P.W. 7 is Biswanath Patra whogsays that he replied

Considering all the facts and circumstances dis- 
cussed above in respect of each and every workman

(1) A “no-dispute” award be passed in respect of
